meta.name: Data APIs & ETL
meta.description: REST endpoints from parameterized SQL and stored procedures, and ETL pipelines between databases

permissions.endpointsRead: See Data APIs, their versions, docs and execution logs
permissions.endpointsManage: Create, edit, test, publish and retire Data APIs
permissions.endpointsInvoke: Call published Data APIs (globally or for one endpoint)
permissions.pipelinesRead: See ETL pipelines and their runs
permissions.pipelinesManage: Create, edit and delete ETL pipelines
permissions.pipelinesRun: Run ETL pipelines now or on a schedule

settings.logRetentionDaysHelp: Data API calls older than this are deleted every night.
settings.defaultRateLimit: Default rate limit (calls per caller per minute)
settings.defaultRateLimitHelp: Used by endpoints that do not set their own limit.

pipeline.name: ETL pipeline
pipeline.description: Runs a Data APIs & ETL pipeline: rows read, written and rejected are reported.

audit.endpoint_draft_loaded: Data API version loaded into the draft
audit.endpoint_access_denied: Data API call refused (API client not allowed)
audit.endpoint_connection_missing: Data API lost its database connection

endpoints.title: Data APIs
endpoints.description: REST endpoints over company databases, built from SQL or stored procedures, versioned and documented.
endpoints.emptyHint: A Data API turns a SQL query or a stored procedure into a documented REST endpoint.
endpoints.liveCount: {count, plural, one {# Data API} other {# Data APIs}}

create.title: New Data API
create.hint: Name it and pick a data connection. You write the SQL (or pick a procedure) next, in the draft.
create.slugInvalid: Lower-case letters, digits and single dashes, starting with a letter
create.slugHint: Callers use /api/v1/etl/data/{slug}. It cannot change once a version is published.
create.connectionHint: Only connections an administrator allowed for data use are listed. Use a least-privilege login.

endpoint.clientsAllowed: {count, plural, =0 {no API clients} one {# API client} other {# API clients}}
endpoint.connectionMissing: The database connection of this Data API was deleted. Pick another connection in the draft and publish a new version.
endpoint.deleteBody: Its versions and execution log are deleted, and callers get 404 from now on.
endpoint.notFound: This Data API does not exist (or was deleted).

statementHint.query: One SQL statement. Values are bound by the driver through :name placeholders, never pasted into the SQL.
statementHint.procedure: A procedure or function from the connection’s catalog; its input arguments become parameters.

editor.sqlHint: Write :name for a parameter. Strings, comments and :: casts are not parameters.
editor.addMissing: {count, plural, one {Add # missing parameter} other {Add # missing parameters}}
editor.writesFound: This SQL changes data or schema ({keywords}). Turn on “Allows writes” to save it.
editor.writesAllowed: This SQL changes data or schema ({keywords}) and is allowed to.
editor.procedureHint: Pick from the routines the connection’s login can see.
editor.cacheHint: 0 turns caching off. Results are cached per version and parameters.
editor.allowsWritesHint: Needed for SQL with write or DDL keywords. Read-only connections refuse writes anyway.
editor.accessHint: Who may call the published versions. Changes apply at once; no new version is needed.
editor.allowUsersHint: People need the permission to call Data APIs, globally or on this endpoint.
editor.noClients: No API clients exist yet. An administrator creates them under Applications & API clients.
editor.rateLimitHint: Leave empty for the default. Now: {n} calls per caller per minute.

params.title: Parameters
params.hint: Typed and validated before the database is called: invalid input is answered with 400 and per-field details.
params.name: Name
params.enumHint: Separate with commas; applied when you leave the field.

test.title: Test console
test.hint: Runs against the real database with these values. A successful test of the draft lets you publish it.
test.manageOnly: Only Data API developers can run tests.
test.empty: Run a test to see rows, columns, the time and the bound SQL.
test.truncated: More rows exist than the limit

publish.title: Publish version {version}
publish.hint: The tested draft is frozen as an immutable version. Callers of the plain URL get it from now on; pinned callers keep theirs.

versions.title: Versions
versions.hint: Published versions never change. Deprecated ones still answer, with a Deprecation header; retired ones answer 410.
versions.none: Nothing is published yet. Test the draft, then publish it.

deprecate.title: Deprecate version {version}?
deprecate.body: It keeps answering, with a Deprecation header and a link to the latest version, so callers can move.

retire.title: Retire version {version}?
retire.body: Calls to it get 410 Gone from now on. You can restore it later.

restore.title: Restore version {version}?
restore.body: It is published again and answers normally.

load.title: Load version {version} into the draft?
load.body: The draft is replaced by this version’s definition. Unsaved edits are lost.

docs.unpublishedHint: Docs appear once a version is published.
docs.requestHint: GET takes the parameters in the query string (lists as repeated keys or comma-separated); POST takes a JSON object.
docs.csvHint: Send Accept: text/csv for CSV. Responses carry RateLimit headers; X-Cache says whether the result came from the cache.

responseHint.rows: data is an array of rows; meta has the row count, whether it was truncated, the version, the time and whether it was cached.
responseHint.single: data is the first row; no matching row answers 404.

docs.authHint: API clients authenticate with an API key or an OAuth client-credentials token. The client must be on this endpoint’s allow-list.

logs.title: Call log
logs.description: Every Data API call: who called which version, the outcome, the time and the rows. Sensitive parameters are masked.
logs.search: Slug, caller, error or request id…
logs.emptyHint: Calls show up here as soon as people or API clients use a published Data API.

pipelines.title: Pipelines
pipelines.description: ETL between database connections: a source query, a target table, column mapping and fixed transforms.
pipelines.newHint: Read from one connection, write to a table of another, in one transaction per run.
pipelines.emptyHint: A pipeline copies rows from a source query into a target table, by hand or on a schedule.

pipeline.incrementalSummary: Incremental on {column}; the next run reads rows after {watermark}.
pipeline.notFound: This pipeline does not exist (or was deleted).
pipeline.runningNow: Running now: {read} rows read, {written} written. View progress
pipeline.deleteBody: The pipeline and its run history are deleted. Data already loaded stays in the target.
pipeline.connectionMissing: A database connection of this pipeline was deleted. Pick another one in the definition.

pipelineEditor.sourceHint: One statement, run read-only and streamed in batches.
pipelineEditor.incrementalHint: Feed :watermark with the highest value of a result column from the last successful run.
pipelineEditor.mappingHint: Source column → target column, with a fixed transform. There is no custom code.
pipelineEditor.noMappings: Map at least one column. Preview the source, then use Auto-map.
pipelineEditor.ownerHint: Told when a run started with Run now fails.
pipelineEditor.targetHint: A table from the target connection’s catalog. Everything is written in one transaction.

modeHint.upsert: Inserts new rows and updates rows with the same key.
modeHint.replace: Deletes all rows of the table, then inserts (in the same transaction).

pipelineEditor.readOnlyTarget: This connection is read-only: pick one that may write.

runs.title: Runs
runs.emptyHint: Use Run now, or schedule the pipeline in Scheduled jobs.

run.title: Run of {name}
run.cancelBody: It stops at the next batch and everything it wrote is rolled back.

links.unavailable: Links and files are not available
links.unavailableHint: The record panels of the platform are not loaded.

taskConfig.hint: Runs the pipeline with the same runner as Run now; rows read, written and rejected appear in the job run.
